newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon says tests New Delhi radar system.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon says tests New Delhi radar system.

text.p: A Raytheon Co spokesman said in a telephone interview from New Delhi, India, that a test of the radar system that the company is installing in that city's airport was successfully completed over the weekend.

Raytheon spokesman Barry French, who is in New Delhi, along with Ron Lewis, manager fo the Lexington, Mass.-based international, high-technology company's air traffic control program in Asia, said he expected system-wide testing of the equipment would begin in early December.
Meanwhile French confirmed that Lewis met with India's director general of civil aviation, H.S. Khola, Wednesday.

Raytheon, which has won a $123 million contract for modernizing and upgrading the Delhi and Mumbai airports' air traffic control systems, came under criticism for not completing the installation sooner. The projects have come under scrutiny after the mid-air collision of a Saudi Boeing Co 747-400 and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 airliner over Chakri Dadri near New Delhi last week.

While the original contract between Raytheon and the Airport Authority of India did call for the installations to be completed by October 1995, both parties agreed to an 11-month extension, French said.

"There are two general reasons for that," said French. One was "there were not sufficient power lines to the area, and the radar building was not complete, so there was a delay in testing it. Also, there had to be some on-site modifications of the radar to satisfy the customer's specifications."
